title: Independent reads and writes
summary: Use a fetcher when an operation should keep the current page and URL.

sections.title: Read a registered route
sections.body: load calls the target loader. Its result goes to fetcher.data and does not replace the page loader data or trigger page revalidation.

sections.title: Mutate a registered route
sections.body: Fetcher forms support POST, PUT, PATCH, and DELETE. Actions target registered routes, not arbitrary unregistered API URLs. A successful action revalidates the active page loader unless shouldRevalidate opts out.

sections.title: State and ownership
sections.body: A fetcher transitions idle → loading → idle for a read; idle → submitting → loading → idle for a successful mutation and revalidation. Each useFetcher instance owns independent data and cancellation. Its data persists during subsequent requests. Errors are exposed as fetcher.error.

sections.title: Navigation versus fetcher
sections.body: Form and Link navigate. fetcher.Form, fetcher.load, and fetcher.submit keep the URL, except when a handler returns a redirect. After a successful mutation, mounted fetchers that have loaded data revalidate their last loaded URL, subject to that route’s shouldRevalidate. Fetchers currently submitting are skipped. Each fetcher still owns its own data; there is no global fetcher cache.

sections.title: load(url): independent reads
sections.body: load selects the loader on a registered route. It changes this fetcher from idle to loading, then back to idle. The returned loader value goes to fetcher.data. It does not navigate or refresh the current page loader. A missing URL defaults to the bound route or current location.

sections.title: GET Form: independent search
sections.body: A fetcher GET form serializes fields into the target URL and loads that route. The browser address does not change. Render the returned search results from this fetcher, rather than useLoaderData. The target loader reads q from request.url.

sections.title: submit(body, options): mutations
sections.body: Pass FormData, an optional action URL, and an uppercase method. The default method is POST. The action result goes to fetcher.data. Successful mutations revalidate the active page loader subject to shouldRevalidate. The returned Promise resolves to a Result with data or error; use fetcher.data for the hook’s inferred result type.

sections.title: Form: declarative mutations
sections.body: The bound Form accepts the same props as Form, including action and lowercase method. It uses this fetcher’s state and data rather than page actionData. Standard named fields and the selected submit button become FormData.
sections.code:
<fetcher.Form action="/tasks/42" method="patch">
  <label>
    Title <input name="title" required />
  </label>
  <button disabled={fetcher.state !== "idle"}>Save</button>
</fetcher.Form>;

sections.title: state: pending UI
sections.body: idle means this channel has no work pending. loading means a read is pending, or page data is being revalidated after an action. submitting means the mutation is pending. A successful write normally moves submitting → loading → idle. Keep controls stable and show a separate status message. Each useFetcher call has independent state.

sections.title: data and error: ownership and lifetime
sections.body: data is initially undefined and retains the previous result while another request is pending. A validation object is data, while an Error is exposed through error. An action result is not the same as the page’s freshly loaded data. There is no global keyed fetcher registry. Mounted fetchers that previously loaded data revalidate their last URL after a successful mutation, subject to shouldRevalidate; unmounted fetchers are disposed.

sections.title: Types and dynamic URLs
sections.body: useFetcher<typeof handler>() derives its data from a specific loader or action. useFetcher(typedRoute) derives a union of the route’s read and mutation results. Narrow that union before reading operation-specific fields. For a bound /tasks/:id route that is not active, pass a concrete URL such as /tasks/42; the router cannot invent id.

sections.title: Concurrency and cleanup
sections.body: Starting another request on the same fetcher aborts its previous request and ignores late completion. Separate fetchers can run concurrently. The framework hook disposes its channel when unmounted. Forward signal from the handler to fetch so cancellation reaches the network. Cancellation does not roll back a write already processed by a backend.

sections.title: Differences to keep in mind
sections.body: This API does not expose React Router’s fetcher.formData, formAction, formMethod, keyed fetchers, or a reset method. Keep any optimistic draft in your own component state and reconcile it with the confirmed result. A redirect returned by an action navigates even though an ordinary fetcher submission stays on the current page.
